newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian zinc output seen up 3.3 pct - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian zinc output seen up 3.3 pct - ABARE.

text.p: Australian zinc mine output is forecast to rise 3.3 percent to 1.11 million tonnes in 1997/98 to June 30 from 1.08 million in 1996/97, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.

In its March quarterly report, ABARE said the production rise in 1997/98 is mainly due to expansion at the existing McArthur River and Woodcutters mines, both in the Northern Territory, and the Elura mine in New South Wales.
MIM Holdings Ltd operates McArthur River, Normandy Mining Ltd owns Woodcutters and Elura is owned by Pasminco Ltd.
ABARE said the expected 1997/98 output rise would also be due to The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's new Cannington mine in Queensland, which is due to start operations in late 1997.

"These production rises are expected to underpin an increase in export volumes, which together with increased prices, are forecast to result in Australian export earnings from zinc increasing by 11 percent in 1996/97 and by a further 27 percent in 1997/98," the government's commodity advisory body said.
The bureau estimates Australia's zinc export value to rise to A$904 million in 1996/97, from A$816 million a year earlier and to rise to A$1.15 billion in 1997/98.

ABARE said world world mine production of zinc is estimated to rise 2.7 percent to 7.22 million tonnes in calendar 1997 and to 7.60 million tonnes in 1998. Zinc metal output is forecast to rise to 7.65 million tonnes in 1998 from 7.47 million in 1997.

The bureau said world mine production of zinc would be boosted by expanded capacity in Australia, Bolivia, Ireland and the United States. It is also expected that the large Faro mine in Canada will reopen in early 1997.
Zinc consumption is set to rebound in calendar 1997 to 7.73 million tonnes after a fall to 7.52 million in 1996. Consumption is estimated to rise to 7.89 million in 1998, ABARE said.

"The main contributing factors to growth in OECD zinc consumption in 1997 are expected stronger automobile production, particularly in the United States, France, Italy and Germany, and some recovery in construction activity in most European countries," ABARE said.
ABARE said in Asia, growth in zinc consumption in 1997 is expected to come from continuing infrastructure development and increased automobile output in South Korea, Taiwan and Malaysia.
Following four years of flat prices, the average world zinc price is expected to rise by 20 percent to US$1,235 per tonne in calendar 1997 and to $1,400 per tonne in 1998, the bureau said.
